Count the days each year above a temperature threshold

Source: R/annual_exceedances.R
annual_exceedances.Rd

For every year, counts the days on which the daily maximum (hot days) or daily minimum (hot nights) temperature was above threshold, restricted to the chosen months. Days without an observation cannot be counted, so the function also reports how much of each year was observed and flags years whose coverage falls below min_coverage. An incomplete year is then not mistaken for a cool one.

Usage

annual_exceedances(
  data = melbheat::melb_temp,
  variable = c("tmax", "tmin"),
  threshold,
  months = 1:12,
  min_coverage = 0.8
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the columns year, month and the column named in variable. Defaults to melb_temp.

variable

Which temperature to use: "tmax" (daily maximum, hot days) or "tmin" (daily minimum, hot nights).

threshold

A single number: the temperature in degrees Celsius. A day counts when its temperature is strictly greater than this value.

months

Integer vector of months to include, 1 (January) to 12 (December). Defaults to the whole year. Years are calendar years, so a summer spanning December to February is split across two years.

min_coverage

A number between 0 and 1. A year is marked reliable when the share of days in the chosen months with an observation is at least this value.

Value

A data frame with one row per year and columns:

year

Calendar year.

n_days

Number of calendar days in the chosen months.

n_observed

Days with a recorded temperature.

n_exceed

Observed days above threshold.

coverage

n_observed / n_days.

prop_exceed

n_exceed / n_observed, or NA if nothing was observed.

reliable

TRUE if coverage >= min_coverage.

The settings used are stored in attr(, "settings") so that summarise_periods(), describe_periods() and plot_exceedances() can label their results without being told again.

Details

Use this function when you need one number per year to compare across time. Do not use the counts of a year marked reliable = FALSE as if they were complete: they are lower bounds.

See also

summarise_periods() to compare two periods and plot_exceedances() to draw the result.

Examples

# Days above 35 degrees, whole year
ex <- annual_exceedances(threshold = 35)
tail(ex)
#>    year n_days n_observed n_exceed  coverage prop_exceed reliable
#> 48 2017    365        365       10 1.0000000  0.02739726     TRUE
#> 49 2018    365        365       11 1.0000000  0.03013699     TRUE
#> 50 2019    365        365       22 1.0000000  0.06027397     TRUE
#> 51 2020    366        366        5 1.0000000  0.01366120     TRUE
#> 52 2021    365        365        4 1.0000000  0.01095890     TRUE
#> 53 2022    365        201        5 0.5506849  0.02487562    FALSE

# Warm nights (minimum above 20 degrees) in December to February
annual_exceedances(variable = "tmin", threshold = 20, months = c(12, 1, 2))
